versions.vendor_benchmark_code: topoteretes/cognee@ba3631f2ed363a6ea50d649c34c56885af6b36fe (tag v1.6.2): cognee/eval_framework/beam/local_ingest.py, preprocessing/preprocess.py (format_turn_pair), report_artifacts/100k_fixed/beam_hybrid_completion_20_20_qa_v1_config.json (the pinned adapter was written from the v1.6.2 files, which v1.6.8 still ships)

entity-h2h.notes: The pinned recipe with LLM_MODEL=openai/gpt-6.2-sol for the entity-resolution head-to-head (newest GPT generation the OpenAI API serves on 2026-11-17), on cognee 1.6.8; the embedder stays at the recipe default. /finish runs consolidate_entities_pipeline once per namespace at the cell's setting (default: similarity_threshold 0.85, its documented default; a tuning or tuned cell: one setting of entity_h2h_tuning) with its other parameters at their defaults (name_match on, top_k 10, allow_cross_type off, protect_node_types none), the memify entity-deduplication step in docs.cognee.ai/guides/memify-entity-deduplication. Structured output: the image sets LITELLM_LOCAL_MODEL_COST_MAP=True, and litellm 1.110.0's bundled model map has no gpt-6.2-sol, so litellm.supports_response_schema is false and cognee's litellm_native adapter takes its JSON fallback for every structured call: response_format json_object with the response model's JSON schema in the system prompt, re-asked with the validation error on a reply that does not validate (native_adapter.py _acreate_json_fallback).

time_notes: Each turn-pair item carries 'Time anchor: <event_time>' in its text, as cognee's BEAM preprocessing does. temporal_cognify stays off, as in cognee's BEAM ingestion; since cognee 1.6.3 the flag is deprecated and ignored, and cognify extracts dates as Timestamp nodes by default. cognee.search takes no query date, so query_time is ignored and applied_settings says so. A null event_time (allowed by the protocol) is written as 'Time anchor: unknown'; cognee never substitutes the ingest time, because dates live only in the text.

provenance.mechanism: Chunk items carry payload.document_id, which is the cognee Data id. The shim pins each session's Data id (uuid5 of namespace and source id) through DataItem.data_id and labels it with the source id, so a chunk maps to exactly one session (exact). Entity and fact items come from the merged graph and carry no source; they are returned with provenance unavailable. The map is rebuilt from cognee.datasets.list_data labels (public API) after a restart.

delete_notes: cognee.forget(data_id, dataset) removes the Data row and its chunks and chunk vectors; after it no chunk from the deleted session returns. In the keyless check (canned extraction), graph entities shared with a surviving session stayed and their edge text still quoted the deleted session; in the metered smoke (real extraction) no entity or fact mentioned the deleted fact. lifecycle-lite should score entity and fact items as well as chunks.
readiness: synchronous: /ingest runs cognee.add then cognee.cognify(run_in_background=False) for that session, as cognee's BEAM local_ingest does, so /finish has nothing to wait for. A failed pipeline raises (raise_on_error=True) and becomes a product_error.
namespace: dataset (one cognee dataset per namespace, named by the opaque ns id; ENABLE_BACKEND_ACCESS_CONTROL is on by default, so each dataset gets its own graph and vector store)

vendor-default.maps_to: cognee.search(query_type=HYBRID_COMPLETION, only_context=True, verbose=True, datasets=[ns]). search top_k 15 caps each hybrid lane at min(15, DEFAULT_HYBRID_LANE_TOP_K=10): 10 chunks, 10 entities with up to 10 edges each, 10 facts. HYBRID_COMPLETION is recall()'s fallback type (ROUTER_FALLBACK_TYPE) and the retriever cognee selected for its reported BEAM configuration. The type is pinned (auto_route off) so the item shape is deterministic.

fixed-evidence.maps_to: cognee.search(query_type=HYBRID_COMPLETION, only_context=True, verbose=True, datasets=[ns]). 20 chunks, 20 entities (cognee's reported BEAM 100K configuration hybrid_completion_20_20_qa_v1), 10 facts; the harness packs the returned items to the 8,000-token budget. Why: the largest documented hybrid setting; the harness truncates to the shared budget

retrieval_notes.item_order: chunks (cognee rank), then entities, then facts, the order cognee renders them into its own context string (raw.context)

agent_surface.version: cognee-mcp 0.5.6 (not built in this lane; Phase 8)

deviations_from_vendor_code: Session documents are added as JSON text through DataItem (with a pinned data_id and the source id as label) instead of a JSON file on disk; JsonListChunker reads the same JSON list either way.
Turns are paired in arrival order (1-2, 3-4, ...) and labelled by speaker; cognee's BEAM code pairs user and assistant turns. LoCoMo has two named speakers and no assistant.
The item header keeps Session/Turn/Time anchor but the session number is the ingestion order inside the namespace, not a dataset session id.

No BEAM turn compression, no session distillation and no global context index: they are BEAM-specific additions in local_ingest.py, not part of add + cognify, and the reported 100K retrieval did not query the global index.

cognee.search with verbose=True is used instead of cognee.recall: for only_context completion types recall returns one rendered prompt string, while search(verbose=True) returns the same retrieval as separate ranked chunks, entities and facts with chunk document ids.
No per-question-type answer prompts: the harness's fixed reader answers.

AMB's cognee provider (vectorize-io/agent-memory-benchmark@f618ed7) ingests all documents then cognifies once and retrieves CHUNKS top 50 with fastembed; this shim follows cognee's own BEAM code instead because it exercises the graph.

entity-h2h only: entity_h2h.py adds OpenAI's wording of the embeddings batch limit ("array length must be 2048 or less") to LiteLLMEmbeddingEngine._EMBED_LENGTH_ERROR_RE, the pattern that sends an over-limit 400 into embed_text's existing split-and-retry path. consolidate_entities embeds every candidate entity name in one request (cognee/tasks/memify/consolidate_entities.py:266 in 1.6.8, unchanged through 1.6.10, no upstream fix or issue as of 2026-11-19), and the pattern covers Vertex's wording of that limit but not OpenAI's, so out of the box the step fails once a graph holds more than 2,048 candidate names. The same names are embedded, in smaller requests; nothing about how entities are merged changes (preregistration Amendment 5). 2026-11-20: batch_limit_check.py now refuses (exit 2) before building an embedder unless every provider key is the compose file's keyless placeholder and the embedding host answers the fake provider's /_stats route, which the metering proxy answers with 404, so it cannot run against a paid stack by mistake.

entity_readout.entities: Entity nodes from get_formatted_graph_data (the dataset graph API)
entity_readout.provenance: DocumentChunk -contains-> Entity, DocumentChunk -is_part_of-> document (id = the per-source data id); exact
entity_readout.merge: consolidate_entities_pipeline collapses each duplicate cluster into one canonical node and deletes the rest; no pointer is kept

entity_h2h_tuning.knob: consolidate_entities_pipeline(similarity_threshold=...), the minimum cosine similarity between two entity-name embeddings for the memify entity-deduplication step to merge them (default 0.85; name_match stays on, its default)
entity_h2h_tuning.notes: The shim passes the setting to consolidate_entities_pipeline in /finish and reports it under GET /health entity_h2h. The grid brackets the 0.85 default: 0.70 toward the guide's own example (0.6), 0.90 to 1.00 toward fewer merges; 1.00 is the largest value the function accepts ((0, 1]). name_match is not in the grid: identical normalised names embed identically (cosine 1.0), so turning it off would not stop a merge any threshold allows. Only the consolidation step reads the knob; entities the extraction itself gives one node are not affected.
